subject: Post-call recap + POC checklist: open-model shortlist & regional fallback plan
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@finco-pay.com>, Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@finco-pay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-08T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + POC checklist: open-model shortlist & regional fallback plan

Hi Alyssa / Ravi —

Thanks again for a great discussion this morning. Quick recap and an actionable POC checklist so we can move to an agreed trial scope next week. I pulled notes from the call and added suggested owners. Please flag anything I missed.

Top priorities you mentioned
- High throughput invoice-parsing + reconciliation assistance (EN + ES).
- Hard requirement: on-prem isolation for transactional dataset during validation window.
- Latency target: median end-to-end < 400ms for short prompts, background batch scoring OK to be higher.
- Quality: entity extraction F1 >= 0.92 on the supplied test set; tolerable hallucination rate <= 1.5%.

Suggested POC success criteria (proposed)
1) Data ingestion: sanitized subset (sample_transactions_subset.csv) ingested into a private S3/VPC-accessible bucket and processed by Redwood Private.
2) Accuracy: entity extraction and label concordance as above on held-out test set; evaluation harness produced by FinCo + Redwood.
3) Performance: 95th pct latency <= 700ms for interactive flows at 10 TPS baseline.
4) Resilience: automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant if larger model misses latency SLOs.
5) Security: KMS-backed keys and audit logs enabled for all trial traffic.

Model shortlist (open models) — initial recommendation- Primary: LlamaX-13B-8bit (good throughput & strong EN/ES transfer)- Contingency (fallback): Mistral-7B-quant (lower latency, smaller memory footprint)- Evaluation-only baseline: BloomZ-7B-mt (to track multilingual degradation)

Multilingual approach- Run primary model for EN and ES. For key Spanish flows, include a prompt-level language tag and compare scores to BloomZ baseline. If ES quality dips > 5% relative to EN, failover to BloomZ-7B-mt for those requests.

Proposed timeline (high level)
- Tue 9/14: SOW + PoC charter agreed (owner: Grace)
- Wed 9/15–9/22: Data ingestion & sandbox setup (owner: Monica)
- Thu 9/23–10/01: Model evaluation runs, initial metrics (owner: Ben)
- Fri 10/08: Readout & acceptance decision (owners: Grace + FinCo)

Immediate asks / next steps- Alyssa / Ravi: confirm acceptance of the success criteria and on-prem requirement by EOD Friday.- FinCo: share secure S3 access details and the sanitized test set (we received sample_transactions_subset.csv but need full subset).- Ben: will spin up initial evaluation harness and share reproducible notebook.- Karthik: will prepare a cost/throughput estimate for both primary and fallback models on Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private.

Attachments: FinCo_PoC_Charter_v1.pdf (draft), sample_transactions_subset.csv (anonymized sample), redwood-poc-sow-draft.docx

Thanks —
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Grace —

Appreciate the thorough recap. High level looks great and aligns with what Ravi and I discussed. A few quick clarifications: 
1) On-prem isolation: we will require the private control plane + a customer-managed VPC; confirm that Redwood Private can deploy to our GCP project (we use GCP in us-central1).
2) Language coverage: Spanish examples are critical — we have a separate Spanish test slice that we'll send.
3) Acceptance gating: can we add a manual QA acceptance step (business team sign-off) in addition to the numeric thresholds?

We'll aim to share the full sanitized subset and VPC details by Monday 9/13. Also attaching a short internal note on compliance expectations (we'll send the formal checklist later).

—Alyssa

- I'll provision the eval harness and run three parallel experiments: LlamaX-13B-8bit (primary), Mistral-7B-quant (fallback), BloomZ-7B-mt (baseline).
- Benchmarks will include token-level latency distribution, end-to-end pipeline timings, and a simple hallucination detector we use in trials.
- Expect first pass results by 9/24. I'll post the notebook to the Drive link once initial runs complete.

If FinCo can provide the Spanish slice and expected label schema (CSV headers), that'll speed things up.

—Ben
